gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 10 build step remains the narrowest honest place to keep the virtio_mmio helper, its dedicated tests, and the survey packet reviewable together.

The existing virtio core lab slice already covers status negotiation, queue callback bookkeeping, bounded queue descriptor-shape metadata, and notification accounting, so the MMIO lane can build on that real foothold instead of inventing a second core starter.
The existing ring survey keeps the queue-wrapper roadmap gap explicit, which the MMIO lane still depends on before transport-facing lifecycle work can honestly widen.
The live repo has a bounded in-memory virtqueue helper for queue shape, queue sizing, notification bookkeeping, and callback pacing, so the MMIO lane can advance against a real queue-facing foothold.
The ring slice note records the bounded queue-helper surface and its remaining non-goals, which keeps the MMIO lane from overstating transport readiness.
The dedicated MMIO survey gate keeps the transport gap explicit and reviewable while the live helper stays intentionally bounded.
The lane needs a Phase 10 note that records the current MMIO transport scope, the live helper-backed surface, and the reasons broader transport work is still blocked.
The live repo now has a tiny in-memory register window for identity reads, queue selection, status reads, and helper-local bookkeeping without widening into lifecycle or probe work.

The same helper already stages queue_num_max, queue_num, and queue_ready in memory, which is the smallest honest queue-size foothold before transport-facing discovery or reset flows. The current tests replay queue_num_max reads and bounded queue programming directly from the helper.
The dedicated MMIO slice note records the landed helper surface and its remaining non-goals so the lane stays reviewable now that the helper is live.

The live helper now carries one bounded device-feature selector and read window so VM-friendly lab validation can replay feature-word reads without widening into interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, or probe lifecycle work.

The same helper now stages one small transport-backed config-word window in memory so VM-friendly lab validation can replay bounded config reads, including the shorter restaged config window that clears stale second-word data and shrinks the readable config window, without implying interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, or probe lifecycle behavior.

The same helper can now summarize one bounded config-word write plan against the staged config window, including the current config generation and previous word value, without mutating config space or claiming interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, or probe lifecycle behavior.

The same helper now summarizes the earliest virtio_mmio_probe()-style preflight checks around identity constants, device presence, vendor presence, legacy guest-page-size intent, bounded queue-register readiness, and interrupt-ack readiness without widening into lifecycle, DMA, or IRQ-delivery parity.

With config-write planning already landed, the live MMIO helper can now summarize which bytes a prepared config-word write would change, including the absolute window end offset and a byte-change mask, without mutating config space or claiming interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, or probe or remove lifecycle behavior.
Interrupt acknowledgement, queue discovery, reset flows, and probe or remove lifecycle behavior remain too transport-facing to start honestly inside this lab helper packet.
